items: Douglas Michael Mallillin was confirmed as the new chairperson of the Commission on Audit (COA) despite initial objections from Senator Imee Marcos regarding the agency's impartiality.

MANILA, Philippines – The Commission on Appointments (CA) on Monday, November 23, confirmed Douglas Michael Mallillin as the new chairperson of the Commission on Audit (COA), despite initial objections from Senator Imee Marcos over the agency’s impartiality.
Mallillin, who was appointed by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. as commissioner in February 2025, will replace former COA chairperson Gamaliel Cordoba who was appointed to the Supreme Court (SC).
Senator Marcos initially moved to defer Mallillin’s confirmation, citing concerns over the COA’s alleged use as an “instrument of political harassment” against members of the opposition.

“For the reason that we require further enlightenment on the vision and mission of the COA that will be effective for accountability in the future, and because the government’s auditing powers should not be wielded selectively against the opposition — the consequences extend far beyond the individual officials immediately affected,” the senator said.
“And the chilling effect threatens the ability of legislators to discharge their constitutional duties without intimidation or political retaliation,” she added.
The senator later withdrew her objection after Mallillin assured the CA that the commission would uphold its constitutional independence.

Under his leadership, Mallillin said he would push for the modernization of government auditing through artificial intelligence (AI), data analytics, and paperless systems to strengthen the detection of irregularities in public spending.
“One of the main programs is actually to upskill and to give the necessary capability to our auditors to audit effectively and efficiently,” Mallillin said.
Mallillin previously served as ad interim COA commissioner and Director IV under the Office of the COA Chairperson.
He also worked as an associate prosecutor at the Department of Justice and deputy commissioner at the National Telecommunications Commission.
Mallillin graduated magna cum laude in accountancy at Saint Louis University in Baguio City. He topped the 1986 Certified Public Accountant Licensure Examination and passed the 1996 Bar Examinations.

In February 2025, the High Court tapped Mallillin to provide expert opinion on the Department of Finance’s (DOF) directive ordering government-owned and controlled corporations, including PhilHealth, to remit excess funds to the National Treasury.

During the oral arguments, justices questioned Mallillin’s explanations, which appeared to align with the DOF’s position on the fund transfer. He was later excused by SC Associate Justice Amy Lazaro-Javier as he “might be charged with partiality or bias” when the case reaches the COA.

In December 2025, the SC ruled that the government must return P60 billion in PhilHealth funds transferred to the National Treasury and permanently prohibited the transfer of the remaining P29.9 billion. The Court also declared the relevant provision of the 2024 General Appropriations Act and DOF Circular No. 003-2024 unconstitutional.

Mallillin was appointed COA commissioner in February 2025 and later confirmed by the CA in June of that year. As COA chairperson, he will serve the unexpired term of Cordoba, which ends on February 2, 2029. – Rappler.com
